reviewedRiskGates.notes: Official page contains all-day, happy-hour, weekend, catering-pizza, and new-food sections; Toast separately exposes regular, summer, and catering catalog sections.
The 127 frozen rows include section/navigation artifacts and omit current Toast-only products; count reconciliation cannot be represented as one exact catalog match.
Frozen records include headings/modifiers and retain older naming/presentation variants; several current Toast products have no frozen row.
Neither accessible source supplies cross-contact or shared-equipment language. The official raw-food warning and GF/V/VG legend are not cross-contact evidence.
Allergen evidence is limited to narrow named-ingredient positives; no complete source supports absence, complete arrays, or cross-contact conclusions.
The scout identified incomplete allergen sourcing; independent review also found incomplete official menu scope and missed current Toast products.

findings.summary: The scout marked the official food page complete and merged all surfaces into one catalog, but the official page does not enumerate the full current catering boundary and Toast contains multiple current unmatched food/catering products.

Frozen positive arrays are labelled official-ingredients although their frozen URLs are Toast ordering URLs. Current restaurant-issued descriptions establish only narrow named-ingredient positives; no complete allergen matrix, negatives, or cross-contact statement was found.
Six frozen rows are menu headings, a category, or a modifier rather than independently orderable food products and should not be reconciled as allergen-bearing menu items.

verifier.summary: Independent verification found material scope, product-boundary, source-authority, and extraction discrepancies. The restaurant identity and Toast location catalog are verified, but the official food page is incomplete for catering, SpotApps is not independently verifiable, five current unmatched Toast product groups were identified, frozen official-ingredient authority is unsupported, and cross-contact remains unresolved.
